question: Which user-facing Dreaming scoping API should OpenClaw support for this issue: per-agent overrides, a memory-core agent allowlist, or pressure/stagger scheduling without per-agent config?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the requested fix adds compatibility-sensitive config surface and the discussion now includes several valid product shapes with different upgrade behavior.

options.title: Accept a scoped allowlist first
options.body: Land a schema-backed memory-core allowlist or equivalent minimum scoping control, then track per-agent schedules separately if still needed.

options.title: Require per-agent overrides
options.body: Keep this issue scoped to agents.list[].dreaming enabled and schedule semantics, accepting a larger agent-config and cron-model change before closure.

options.title: Defer config to scheduler pressure work
options.body: Avoid new per-agent config for now and handle overload with pressure backoff or stagger behavior, leaving opt-out use cases unresolved.

recommendation.title: Accept a scoped allowlist first
recommendation.body: Land a schema-backed memory-core allowlist or equivalent minimum scoping control, then track per-agent schedules separately if still needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and history put this person closest to the config schema, memory-host resolver, and Dreaming docs surfaces that need the product/API decision.
